verdict.rationale: Gitea's own docs show it is a self-hosted service that installs on your own servers from a binary or the official container image. Configuration works through the admin panel or app.ini, and community reports describe painless installs and simple binary-swap upgrades. Upgrade and ongoing maintenance are not documented first-party, and a community question about backup and restore leaves maintenance coverage incomplete. Missing for 10: first-party upgrade/migration documentation, documented backup/restore and maintenance procedures, independent corroboration of long-term maintenance at scale.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can install, configure, upgrade, and maintain my own instance on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Free, self-hosted Git service under the MIT license. Full control, unlimited users and repositories.
or use container (docker/podman/etc) to deploy on your own server with the official image.
For static config options, you can edit your app.ini file and restart the instance.
It can be easily deployed on various servers without complex configurations or dependencies.
Upgrades are super simple: stop the service, replace the single binary, start it again.
